title: A Atlas for the Harbor
premise: In the winter of 1918, in a fog-bound harbor city, Felix Joubert — a woman passing as a man to keep her dead master's mapmaking trade alive — races to complete the coastal atlas he died protecting. When she finds a sealed letter hidden in his drafting table naming her own family among conspirators plotting to sabotage the armistice negotiations, Felix must choose between burning the evidence and delivering it through three military checkpoints controlled by men who would hang her for what she carries. Along the way she falls for Lieutenant Arnaud Vasseur, assigned to guard the very checkpoint she must deceive, forcing love and duty into open war. In the end Felix delivers the atlas and the letter together at the signing itself, exposing the plot, claiming her name and her trade openly, and choosing Arnaud not as an escape from duty but as a duty of her own making.
about_author: Edmund Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing harbor charts and armistice-era correspondence before turning to fiction. A Atlas for the Harbor is a second novel informed by that quiet life among other people's letters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She works alone in the dead master Perrin's studio, finishing plate forty-one of the harbor atlas while the city waits on armistice news. Establishes her disguise, her debts, and her belief that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking fear.

chapters.title: What the Master Left Undrawn
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inventorying Perrin's effects for the guild, she finds a sealed letter sewn into the backing of an old chart, addressed in his hand but never sent. She almost burns it unread. Beat: dread disguised as tidiness.

chapters.title: A Name She Wasn't Given
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The letter names three families — hers included — in a plot to delay or destroy the armistice by striking the harbor's signal station. Her brother Émile's signature is on an attached pledge. Beat: the floor giving way beneath certainty.

chapters.title: The Guild of Careful Men
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Ozenne's POV. The guild debates whether to certify an atlas finished by 'Perrin's boy,' revealing how fragile Felix's disguise is and how much Ozenne suspects. Beat: menace wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Ink Gate
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Carrying survey plates toward the naval archive, she passes her first checkpoint and observes its routines with a mapmaker's eye — noting Lieutenant Arnaud Vasseur, who catches her staring too long. Beat: first spark of danger that feels like recognition.

chapters.title: Émile at the Door
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. Felix confronts her brother; he defends the conspiracy as patriotism owed to their father's memory. He warns her the letter makes her complicit either way. Beat: family love curdling into threat.

chapters.title: The Cartography of Lying
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She drafts two versions of everything — true charts and altered ones — deciding deception requires the same precision as truth. First plan to move the letter forms. Beat: cold resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Tea with Madame Roux
chapters.summary: Madame Roux's POV. A widow of one named family begs Felix to destroy the evidence rather than ruin the survivors. Offers money; offers silence. Beat: guilt arriving wearing kindness.

chapters.title: The Lieutenant's Rounds
chapters.summary: Arnaud's POV. Arnaud walks Checkpoint One, bored and homesick, and can't stop thinking about the apprentice with ink-stained fingers. He requests the atlas inspection detail. Beat: longing mistaken for professional curiosity.

chapters.title: Plate Forty-One
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Completing the final plate, she realizes Perrin hid coordinates of the signal station inside the decorative border — the atlas itself is half the evidence. Beat: awe and horror at her master's foresight.

chapters.title: Midnight Survey
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She surveys the signal station under pretext of finishing the chart, confirming the conspirators' target and timing. Nearly caught by a sentry. Beat: terror sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Ozenne's Offer
chapters.summary: Ozenne's POV. The guildmaster reveals he knows 'Felix' is a woman and offers protection in exchange for the letter — to use it for the guild's leverage. Beat: refuge revealed as another cage.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Customhouse
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She tests the customhouse checkpoint with a decoy parcel, mapping its weaknesses. Arnaud appears there too, transferred, and they share a real conversation about maps and home. Beat: warmth blooming inside surveillance.

chapters.title: Letters Never Meant for Me
chapters.summary: Arnaud's POV. Sorting intercepted mail, Arnaud reads a fragment mentioning 'the harbor families' and reports it up the chain — unknowingly starting a clock against Felix. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Pledge of Three Families
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. The conspirators meet in the Joubert cellar; Émile wavers when he sees his sister's name added to the roster without consent. Beat: conscience flickering under loyalty.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Chart Shop
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Arnaud visits the shop officially; over tea they talk until dark. Felix lies about small things and hates how easily he believes her. Beat: love as a complication she didn't budget for.

chapters.title: Burning Is Also a Choice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Alone with the letter over a candle, she weighs destroying it — sparing Émile, sparing herself, betraying Perrin. She cannot do it. Beat: the moral fulcrum of the book.

chapters.title: The Widow's Warning
chapters.summary: Madame Roux's POV. Roux, terrified, tips off the conspirators that the apprentice has the letter. Now Felix is hunted by the people she's trying to save from themselves. Beat: safety collapsing.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two, Again
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Smuggling the letter sewn into a rolled chart, she passes the customhouse by seconds as inspectors tear apart the cart behind her. Arnaud waves her through, then doubts. Beat: triumph laced with guilt.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Arnaud's POV. Questioned about the fragment he reported, Arnaud realizes the trail leads toward the mapmaker's apprentice. He says nothing — his first act of treachery. Beat: duty bending.

chapters.title: What Father Signed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She deciphers their late father's correspondence and learns Perrin discovered the plot years ago and died keeping it. Her inheritance is not property but obligation. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reconnaissance of the citadel gate where the armistice delegation will pass — the only route to reach the signatories. It is impassable. Beat: despair at the wall of the world.

chapters.title: Ozenne Moves First
chapters.summary: Ozenne's POV. The guildmaster leaks word of the letter to force the conspirators' hand, intending to buy the guild's future with chaos. Beat: ambition as arson.

chapters.title: Raid on the Studio
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Conspirators ransack the shop hunting the letter; Felix hides in the chart drawers, hearing Émile's voice among them, denying she has it. Beat: betrayal made physical.

chapters.title: The Confession at the Breakwater
chapters.summary: Arnaud and Felix, dual POV. On the breakwater, each nearly tells the truth; neither does. They agree to meet after the armistice, when 'everything will be simpler.' Beat: tenderness built on a fault line.

chapters.title: Émile's Choice
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. Ordered to silence the apprentice permanently, Émile instead warns Felix to flee the city by morning. Beat: love winning one last time against duty.

chapters.title: Flight Through the Fog
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She tries to leave and cannot — the atlas is due to the archive, and an unfinished atlas is a lie. She turns back at the city limits. Beat: identity asserting itself.

chapters.title: Arrested Attention
chapters.summary: Arnaud's POV. Arnaud detains Felix at Checkpoint One on suspicion, then releases her off the record, demanding the truth. She gives him half of it. Beat: trust gambled between enemies.

chapters.title: The Plan of Three Gates
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. With Arnaud's unwitting help mapped out, she designs the run: decoy at the ink gate, bribe at the customhouse, and the citadel passed inside the official atlas delivery itself. Beat: hope engineered like a bridge.

chapters.title: Madame Roux's Debt
chapters.summary: Madame Roux's POV. Roux, ashamed, gives Felix her husband's old courier credentials — the key to the customhouse passage. Beat: redemption purchased with borrowed courage.

chapters.title: The Night Before Signing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She finishes the atlas, seals the letter inside the cover binding, and writes her true name on the title page: Félicie Joubert. Beat: quiet, trembling self-acceptance.

chapters.title: Gate One Falls
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The decoy parcel is caught at the ink gate exactly as planned; the searchers congratulate themselves while the real cargo rolls past. Beat: nerve held by a thread.

chapters.title: Gate Two and the Cost
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the customhouse, Roux's credentials fail under a new inspector; Felix buys passage with Perrin's silver instruments — surrendering her master's tools, her livelihood. Beat: sacrifice made tangible.

chapters.title: Gate Three: The Citadel
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Inside the official delivery cart, she reaches the citadel — and finds Arnaud waiting, ordered to inspect every case personally. Beat: the collision she dreaded arrives.

chapters.title: Everything Will Be Simpler
chapters.summary: Arnaud and Felix, dual POV. He opens the atlas, sees the letter, sees her face, and understands everything at once. He lets her pass — and chooses to walk beside her. Beat: love choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Amid the ceremony, Felix places the atlas and letter before the delegates; the plot is exposed mid-signature, arrests following quietly so the armistice holds. Beat: history happening to her, finally, on purpose.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Émile surrenders and is spared for his warning; Ozenne's leverage evaporates; Roux mourns and is thanked. Each character pays or receives what they earned. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: The Atlas Published
chapters.summary: Félicie's POV. The atlas is issued under both names — Perrin's and hers — and the guild certifies a woman mapmaker for the first time. Beat: inheritance claimed, not inherited.

chapters.title: Charting New Water
chapters.summary: Félicie's POV. She reopens the studio, takes an apprentice of her own, and begins a new survey of the harbor as it changes in peacetime. Beat: work as healing.

chapters.title: An Atlas for the Harbor
chapters.summary: Félicie's POV, closing. On the breakwater with Arnaud, she looks at the city she once thought history ignored. Identity, love, and duty no longer at war — drawn, at last, on the same map. Beat: peace earned, not given.
